summary: PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18 extracts Dasgupta–Kakde–Ventullo, On the Gross–Stark conjecture (Ann. of Math. 188 (2018) 833–870). It has 125 items (2 library, 14 planned, 109 missing), 4 routes and 35 source issues, after a heavy four-checker review. Its prerequisites match the paper's 24 references, and its Gross–Stark-specific content has a single owner. Four findings: two medium, two low. (1, medium, duplicate) Route 1's brief does not import IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants. So the Part II would plan again the generic content of §4, which IHG.1 and IHG.4 plan: the generalized matrix algebra with residually distinct characters, the extension module B and the class κ, and Chebotarev-plus-continuity integrality. The review's own item notes say to import IHG and that the brief omits it, but the brief was not changed. The Brumer–Stark side (I.7 and PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-23) already imports that machinery from IHG. (2, medium, error) The review put its new item on the two-character Eisenstein series E_k(ψ, η) and the family E(χ, 1) on route 2. That route's only stage is AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L0, a ray-class-character layer. The Hilbert Eisenstein series, including this paper's own E_k(1, η) and E(1, χ), are planned at L3. (3, low) Route 1's reason and brief describe IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.3 as building the Deligne–Ribet L-function, and two items list I.3 as a planner. RS-16, accepted eight hours before the review, narrowed I.3 to a normalization dictionary. (4, low) There is no sourceVersions list.
checked: Independence: the extraction is by Claude Code cc-d67081 and its review by Claude Code cc-39fac3 (issue #1148). This worker (Claude Code, cc-c2c06b) did neither, and did not touch PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-23, IntegralIwasawaTheory or IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants.

Downloaded the published PDF on 2026-09-30 (SHA-256 974e6427…b659, matching the extraction and the review). Compared its 24 references with the 24 prerequisites: they match one for one, so no source the paper builds on is missing.

Read every route, its reason and brief, and all 125 items' statuses in the repository at 14e0fb4d. Read the stage texts, and every restructuring decision on them, in the assembled atlas (2840 stages, 8007 edges). The stages are IntegralIwasawaTheory I.3 (RS-16 narrow), I.5, I.6 and I.7; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L0 and L3 (RS-14 narrow); DirichletPadicLFunctions L3 (RS-14 narrow); PadicFamilies L0a and L5; OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.3 (RS-08 narrow); ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4 and D7 (RS-08 narrow); and IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.1, IHG.4 and IHG.6. All 14 stage ids the extraction cites (planned lists and route stages) exist in the assembled atlas, and none was dropped. Findings 2 and 3 are about the layers' scope, not their existence.

Duplication: went through the item list of PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-23 (235 items), reading its §§8–9 Hilbert-modular, Eisenstein and Ribet items (roughly 172–292) in full, and compared them with this paper's §§3–4. DK23 plans the Hilbert-modular steps of the generalized Ribet method at I.7 and IHG.6, and its Eisenstein series at AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3 (findings 1 and 2). Searched every other extraction for Gross–Stark, Gross's regulator, L-invariants and the id IntegralIwasawaTheoryPartII: no other paper plans them, so the Part II's Gross–Stark-specific content (regulator, orthogonality, Artin rings W_1–W_3, the determinant) has one owner.

Packets: the AutomorphicPadicLFunctions packet (19 nodes; L0 partial, L3 not_read) and the PadicFamilies packet (72 nodes; L5 partial) do not yet cite this paper. So routes 2 and 4 have not been carried out, and route 2 can still be corrected.

Library: Mathlib 082e2d3 has NumberField.Units.rank, unitLattice_rank, finrank_modTorsion, analyticOrderAt, iteratedDeriv, cyclotomicCharacter (Cyclotomic/CyclotomicCharacter.lean:307, with continuity at :336) and IsAdicComplete.henselianRing. Tau Ceti f790474 has TauCeti.teichmuller (LocalField/Teichmuller.lean:100). The review's notes already point to cyclotomicCharacter and the Hensel input, and the two library items say what they claim.

Checked m-ideal: m is a height-one prime with T/m ≅ E of characteristic 0. So the paper's Ribet step is the residually distinct case, which IHG.1 owns; IHG.6 is the non-distinct branch. Finding 1 names both accordingly.

Did not re-verify the 35 source issues: the review checked each at its locator on page images, with four checkers. I read the E18 correction in the brief against the statement of item theorem-3-2 only.

findings.claim: The review added one item to route 2, whose only stage is L0: 'The Eisenstein series E_k(ψ, η) and the Hida family E(χ, 1)'. It gives their Fourier coefficients, Hecke eigenvalues and the congruence mod π. L0 is 'Ray-class character spaces and evaluation', a layer of characters, their avatars, conductors and local factors. Route 2's reason covers only the L-function of χ, its Euler factors and L(χ, 0) ≠ 0, and does not mention the new item. Hilbert Eisenstein series belong to L3: RS-14 narrows L3 to keep 'Hilbert Eisenstein construction on canonical geometric objects, integral congruences'. This extraction's own sister items eisenstein-series (E_k(1, η)) and eisenstein-family (E(1, χ)) are planned at L3. The accepted PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-23 plans the S-stabilised Eisenstein series E_k(ψ_S, 1) and its constant terms at L3 (with I.3). As routed, the L0 blueprint is asked to build an Eisenstein family it does not plan, and the L3 blueprint, which does, is not told about it. The AutomorphicPadicLFunctions packet has not yet taken it up: L0 is partial and L3 not_read, so the route can still be corrected before it takes effect.
findings.evidence: Item rev-the-eisenstein-series-e-k (locator '§3.2, (29)–(30), pp. 848–849 …'): 'For narrow ray class characters ψ, η … E_k(ψ, η) ∈ M_k(ab, ψη) has normalised coefficients c(m, E_k(ψ, η)) = Σ_{r | m} ψ(m/r) η(r) Nr^{k−1} … There is E(χ, 1) ∈ M^o(n, χ) with ν_k(E(χ, 1)) = E_k(χ, ω^{1−k}) … It is a Hecke eigenfamily …'. Its note: 'Route: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions.' Route 2: stages ['AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L0']; reason 'The complex L-function of the ray-class character attached to χ, its Euler factors … and the non-vanishing L(χ, 0) ≠ 0 … L0 owns ray-class characters, their algebraic and p-adic avatars, conductors and local factors; L3 then builds the p-adic L-function'. Atlas stage L0: '## L0. Ray-class character spaces and evaluation. Construct the inverse limit of ray class groups … Develop locally algebraic Hecke characters, their algebraic and p-adic avatars …'. RS-14 layers['AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3'].keeps: 'Own Deligne–Ribet over general totally real F: algebraicity of partial zeta values, Hilbert Eisenstein construction on canonical geometric objects, integral congruences, bounded denominators, smoothing and Euler factors'. Items eisenstein-series and eisenstein-family: planned ['AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3']. PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-23 items 208 ('S-stabilised Eisenstein series E_k(ψ_S, 1)', planned L3 and I.3) and 211 ('E_k(ψ_S, 1) is a Hecke eigenform …', planned L3). research/blueprint/packets/AutomorphicPadicLFunctions.json coverage: L0 partial, L3 not_read, and no node cites this paper.
